title: Land a bare stranded wire in a push-in terminal using the operating tool
instruction: Land the blue wire's stripped end in terminal X1:4, the blue terminal, upper entry. The strands have no ferrule: push the green operating tool into X1:4's operating slot to open the clamp, insert the wire until the insulation stops, then pull the tool out and let go.
context: Fine-stranded wire without a ferrule cannot be pushed into a push-in terminal: an electrician opens the clamp with a small screwdriver in the slot next to the entry, inserts the wire and withdraws the tool. A wire in the wrong terminal puts a conductor on the wrong circuit, and a tool left in the slot leaves the clamp open, so the wire is not held; electricians tug every wire after landing it.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Plate: a light-grey 3 mm steel mounting plate (23 cm wide, 26 cm tall) stands upright on the table, fixed to it, its front face 32.5 cm in front of the bases, spanning 20 cm right to 3 cm left of the midline. A steel EN 60715 TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail runs left-right across it, centre 14.9 cm above the table. Terminals: six WAGO TOPJOB S 2-conductor feedthrough terminal blocks (polyamide, 5.2 mm wide, 48.5 mm long, front face 32.9 mm above the rail) stand side by side on the rail, long side vertical, front faces 28.5 cm in front of the bases, upper ends 17.75 cm above the table. From left to right they are X1:1, X1:2 and X1:3 (grey, 2002-1201), X1:4 (blue, 2002-1204), X1:5 (green-yellow, 2002-1207) and X1:6 (grey, 2002-1201). X1:1 is centred 6.8 cm right of the midline and they step right by 5.2 mm, so X1:4 is centred 8.4 cm right. A WAGO 2002-1291 end plate closes the right end, and end stops sit at both ends. Each block carries a white printed marker (1 to 6) in the middle of its front face, and the left end stop carries the group marker X1. Each block's lower entry already holds a 1.5 mm2 wire with a black ferrule (X1:1 brown, X1:2 black, X1:3 grey, X1:4 blue, X1:5 green-yellow, X1:6 brown), running down into the duct. Each upper entry is an empty hole in the front face, 4 mm below the upper end, angled 15 degrees downward into the block; 8.4 mm below each entry's centre is the block's operating slot, a 4 x 1.2 mm rectangular opening that runs straight into the face. Duct: a grey slotted PVC wiring duct (4.5 cm deep, 6.7 cm tall) is fixed to the plate below the terminals, 3.25 to 9.9 cm above the table, spanning 1.5 to 14.7 cm right of the midline. Wire: a 2.5 mm2 fine-stranded conductor (H07V-K) with blue PVC insulation (3.6 mm across), 40 cm long from the duct, its end stripped 10 mm with no ferrule (bare copper strands). It leaves the duct through a slot in its bottom wall 14 cm right of the midline and 29 cm in front of the bases, drops to the table, runs back toward the robot and left to about 4 cm right of the midline and 7 to 12 cm in front of the bases, rises, and turns right onto the stand. Stand: a dark-grey plastic stand (two posts 2 x 16 mm with low side lips) centred 17 cm in front of the bases and 13 cm right of the midline. The wire's last 8 cm of insulation lies on it pointing forward and sloping 15 degrees down like the entry, the bare strands beyond the front post, the insulation's front end 9.3 cm above the table. Tool: a WAGO 210-720 operating tool (screwdriver: blade 3.5 x 0.5 mm and 10 mm long, 3 mm shaft partly sleeved in green, 13 mm green handle, 19 cm long overall) lies level on a second dark-grey stand of two posts (2 x 20 mm, one under the shaft and one under the handle, with low side lips), pointing forward with the blade's 3.5 mm width horizontal, its axis 9.25 cm above the table and 2 cm left of the midline, the blade's tip 27 cm in front of the bases.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, the stripped end's tip goes more than 1 mm into any terminal entry other than X1:4's upper entry, or if, at the end, the tool's blade is in any operating slot (more than 1 mm past the face). Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the tool's blade is in X1:4's operating slot holding its clamp open (a 2.5 mm2 test strand slides in past the clamping point with no resistance; in the simulator, the clamping spring's leg opened 20 degrees or more); 0.5 if, with the tool still holding the clamp open, the stripped end then goes 7.5 mm or more into X1:4's upper entry; 0.75 if the wire is then seated: the insulation within 1 mm of the entry's mouth, the strands' tip 8.5 mm or more in, the tool out of every slot, and the clamp closed on the strands; 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. Dropping the wire or the tool is not penalised by itself. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the wire end for 1 s (or at the end of the run): mark the insulation with a pen at the entry's mouth, then pull the wire end straight back out along the entry's axis with a spring scale, raising the pull to 50 N over 0.5 s and holding it for 1.5 s. It passes if the mark moves out less than 1.5 mm. If it fails, the score is 0.75. Damage to the strands (splayed or cut strands) is not scored. Distances are read with a rule, or from a close-up photo with a scale in view.
reset_notes: Push the operating tool into X1:4's operating slot to open the clamp, pull the wire out and withdraw the tool. Twist the strands back together if they splayed (re-strip 10 mm if any are bent or cut). Lay the wire end back on its stand with the strands forward and the cable along its starting path from the duct slot, and lay the tool back on its stand, blade forward and flat. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX at 480 Hz, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Published: block sizes, entry angle, strip length, tool blade. Clamp is a sprung hinged leaf (stand-in for CAGE CLAMP); stripped end is sprung strand links that bunch if pushed alone. Slot, ramp, springs, friction inferred from photos and tuned. Tool less self-holding than real (demo keeps hold). Square colliders; wire is jointed capsules; target told by blue housing; 50 N pull in sim after recording. Details in README.
